1.what: The Act has short title as Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 and extends to all of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

3.what: A banker includes a person who is engaged in the business of banking, whether as an individual or as a firm or company.

15.what: This section states that the Bare Act is a government source available in the public domain, and it is being used strictly for educational purposes only.

16.what: A document that is endorsed with the words ‘in blank’ or ‘in full’ is called an ‘indorsement’.

21.what: This section states that a person can be charged with an offence if they are caught at the scene of the crime (‘at sight’) or if they are found to have been involved in the crime after it has happened (‘after sight’).

25.what: When day of maturity is a holiday

40.what: The liability of an indorser is discharged when the principal debt becomes void or is satisfied.

45A.what: The holder has the right to a duplicate of a lost bill.

59.what: A document that proves you paid for accommodation, such as a note or bill, is evidence of payment if it was given to the person who provided the accommodation.

60.what: This section states that an instrument (e.g. a contract) is negotiable until payment or satisfaction is made.

67.what: A person who has issued a promissory note that is payable by instalments must present to the court, within one month of the due date, an account of all payments made and any interest accrued.

69.what: This section does not state anything. It is a placeholder for the actual text of Section 69, which is missing.

77.what: A banker is liable for negligently dealing with a bill presented for payment.

81.what: If you pay for a bill or note, the person giving it to you must deliver it to you. If they don't, and you lose it, you can still get your money back.

82.what: A person who has committed an offence can be discharged from liability if the offence is cancelled, they are released, or they pay a fine.

87.what: If a person makes a material alteration to an instrument, they are guilty of an offence.

90.what: This section states that rights of action on a bill can be extinguished if it is accepted by the acceptors in their hands.

98.what: When notice of dishonour is unnecessary

100.what: A person is guilty of an offence if, without lawful authority or reasonable excuse, they intentionally or recklessly obstructs a constable in the execution of his duty.

107.what: A person who is required to give a notice under this Chapter must give it within a reasonable time.

115.what: In any case where it appears to the court that a bill of exchange, promissory note or other written instrument has been drawn by a person who is incapable of drawing it, or that it has been delivered through mistake or accident, the court may order the drawee to pay the amount due on the instrument.

116.what: Acceptance of a bill or note without protest is not considered an acceptance of the debt.

117.what: No person shall be entitled to any compensation for the death of a child under the age of 18, except in accordance with this Chapter.

118.what: Presumptions as to negotiable instruments: The following presumptions apply - (a) the consideration for an instrument is valid; (b) the date of an instrument is the date on which it was issued or drawn; (c) the time of acceptance of an instrument is the time when it was presented; (d) the time of transfer of an instrument is the time when it was delivered; (e) the order of indorsements on an instrument is as stated in the instrument; (f) the stamp on an instrument is genuine; (g) that a person holding an instrument is a holder in due course.

122.what: A person who has signed a document is estopped from denying that they signed it, and from claiming that they did not have the capacity to sign it.

126.what: Payment of a cheque that is crossed 'specially' means that the cheque has been marked with a special mark or code, indicating that it should only be cashed at a specific bank or financial institution.

131A.what: This section states that Chapter applies to drafts.
